note: Three power chords as one shape moved to three roots on the low E string: the chord boxes first, then a strum-along with a down on every beat. The chords are the riff, so only the tempo moves (60 to 90 bpm); the why says what makes a riff of one shape work, and the block ends on a feel to reach.

exercise.title: E5, G5, A5 riff
exercise.why: A power chord is the same shape on any root, so a riff of power chords is one hand shape slid along the low strings to each new root.

cells.text: Press a chord box below to hear it and see where it sits. All three are one power chord shape, moved to three roots on the low E string.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the metronome at {{=bpm}}. After a bar of count-in, the lit box shows the chord to play: strum down on every beat, one bar for each chord.
Practice until the slide from one root to the next lands on beat 1 with the shape still held.
